entities.summary: Abdul Rahman bin Ibrahim al-Munif, also known as Abdelrahman Munif, was a novelist, short story writer, memoirist, journalist, thinker, and cultural critic. He is considered one of the most significant authors in the Arabic language of the 20th century. His novels include strong political elements as well as mockeries of the Middle Eastern elite classes. He is best-known for Cities of Salt, a quintet of novels about how the discovery of oil transformed a traditional Bedouin culture. Munif's work offended the rulers of Saudi Arabia, which led to the banning of many of his books and the revocation of his Saudi Arabian citizenship.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Abdul Rahman Munif's novels, particularly 'Cities of Salt', had a significant impact on regional literature and culture in West Asia, offering a critique of Middle Eastern elite classes and the effects of oil discovery on traditional Bedouin cultures. His work has been widely studied and translated, contributing to a deeper understanding of the region's complexities.
